title: Timely appointments
context: Wait times, opening hours and acceptance of new patients determine when care is available.
role: The program includes a sponsored direct primary care membership and ongoing telehealth.
limits: Provider counts do not measure appointment availability. Routine and urgent care, and new and established patients, can face different waits.
source: Appointment access and patient experience: AHRQ CAHPS.

title: Workforce capacity
context: Provider availability depends on the number and mix of clinicians, where they practice and whether they accept new patients.
role: The program provides access to a direct primary care membership with Dr. Michael Purcell and Purcell Integrative Osteopathic Care.
limits: Workforce ratios and shortage designations describe capacity. They do not measure an individual practice’s open appointments.
source: HRSA, fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.

title: Affordable care
context: Out-of-pocket costs, coverage gaps and time away from paid work can make it difficult to obtain and continue care.
role: The program sponsors a direct primary care membership and includes help with transportation. Membership is not health insurance.
limits: Insurance coverage and affordability are different measures. Coverage alone does not establish whether someone can afford the care they need.

title: Usable technology
context: Telehealth depends on a usable connection, a suitable device, digital skills, accessibility and a private place to speak.
role: Ongoing telehealth and health access education are included in the program.
limits: An internet subscription does not establish connection quality, digital confidence or telehealth readiness.
source: Computer and internet access: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey.

title: Practical access
context: Distance, transportation, disability access, work schedules and caregiving responsibilities shape whether people can reach care. Food and housing insecurity add to daily demands.
role: The program includes help with transportation.
limits: Transportation and food-insecurity measures describe different barriers. Food insecurity concerns reliable access to enough food; it is not a measure of a local food-supply shortage.
source: Transportation and food insecurity: CDC PLACES.

title: Navigation and continuity
context: Language, health literacy, trust, referrals and follow-up shape whether people can understand the process and remain connected to care.
role: The program includes health access education and coordination. Clinical care remains with the licensed provider.
limits: County-level statistics do not describe an individual’s experience, trust or understanding.
